title: LM-7 cabin mechanisms and crew-provision evidence follow-up
status: SOURCE EVIDENCE ONLY - not merged into the frozen 585-entry inventory

scope.meaning: All numbered rows in AOH figures 2.11-15 and 2.11-16 have a disposition below. Rows are packages or assemblies, overlap between arrangements, and are not a count of independent controls.
scope.remainingReason: Wearable/EVA hardware, CSM-side tunnel hardware, stowage closures and exact mechanism geometry require an explicit scope and additional drawings. The evidence establishes specific omitted mechanisms, not an exhaustive new vehicle control total.

aoh.title: Apollo Operations Handbook, LM 7 and Subsequent, Volume 1, LMA790-3-LM
aoh.pageNumbering: pdfPage is one-based; printedPage is the printed handbook leaf
aoh.review: Visual review of rendered pages; OCR was used only as a finding aid
aoh.applicabilityCaution: The list of illustrations calls figure 2.11-16 an LM 6 arrangement. The foldout is dated 1 February 1970 and drawing 300LM7-2. Its placements are generic handbook evidence; the mission-specific list below adjudicates selected Apollo 13 stowage facts.

controller_report.title: NASA TN D-7884, Apollo Experience Report, Crew Station Integration, Volume III, Spacecraft Hand Controller Development
controller_report.geometryCaution: Table V is CM Block II THC, not LM TTCA. Generic appendix stop requirements do not replace LM-7 AOH values.

as13_stowage.title: Apollo Stowage List, Mission AS 508 CM 109/LM-7, Apollo 13, Final Release
as13_stowage.review: Cover and PDF pages 49, 56 and 58 visually reviewed
as13_stowage.dateCaution: The URL filename suggests July; the cover and reviewed leaves explicitly date the document 21 April 1970 and state that it documents the as-launched configuration, with the CM entry list revised.

facts.fact: One water dispenser/fire extinguisher, part 14-0131-01, on W20 hose at the ECS heat exchanger.
One emergency wrench B, V36-601400-21, in RHSSC.
Two utility lights with cord and clamp, LDW340-53053-3-6, one per interim-stowage pocket.
One interim stowage assembly installed in front of center instrument panel.
Two hammock assemblies stowed under LHSSC, one designated CDR.

mechanismGroups.interaction: Remove cap and secure to mount. Rotate local intensity control clockwise until reticle appears, then adjust brightness. Figure identifies barrel lock and mounting track; snap-on filter is separately stowed.

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: OFF/DIM/BRIGHT selectors present; lamps, plugs and clamps absent
mechanismGroups.interaction: Portable lamp with cord and clamp. Position/orientation is a movable-object pose, not a fixed aiming knob with invented detents.

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: lighting switches/dimmers present; reflector aiming absent
mechanismGroups.interaction: Rotate overhead floodlight reflectors. The handbook names two overhead and two forward fixtures, but explicitly attributes rotatable reflectors only to the overhead lights.

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: absent; distinct from both ACA grip PTT entries
mechanismGroups.interaction: PTT switches are named on the commander and LM pilot oxygen umbilical assemblies. Precise button form and stroke are not specified by this stowage row.
notEstablished: part number and separate reference designator

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: ECS suit isolation valves present; crew quick-disconnect connections absent
mechanismGroups.interaction: Separate oxygen, electrical and water umbilicals serve each astronaut. Oxygen uses two hoses, dual-passage ECS connector and separate supply/exhaust PGA hoses. ECS end stays attached when PGA disconnected.
notEstablished: connector release motion and collar angles

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: absent
mechanismGroups.interaction: Coiled hose and trigger dispenser on mounting bracket; existing DES H2O or ASC H2O valve permits water flow. PDF446 explicitly identifies both as dispenser feeds, so no extra feed-valve definition is missing. Water is also used for fire extinguishing. Tool B is identified for use with the dispenser, but this section does not specify its exact servicing operation.

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: absent
mechanismGroups.interaction: Modified Allen-head L wrench with ball-lock head retention. Identified uses include probe/drogue, descent battery removal, CM hatch and dispenser.

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: absent
sourceStates: secured in three tunnel mounting lugs
mechanismGroups.interaction: Handles release the three-section aluminum cone from tunnel mounts; removal is possible from either end of the tunnel. Three mounting lugs do not establish the exact count or travel of release handles.

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: 11 hatch definitions present; quick-release hinge pins and antibacterial filter absent
mechanismGroups.interaction: Forward hatch is inward swinging, cam-latched, has interior/exterior handles, emergency lockpin and quick-release hinge pins. Filter is stowed on its inside and fitted to relief/dump valve for lunar EVA depressurization. Overhead hatch unlatches by about 90 degrees counterclockwise inside, clockwise outside; cabin must first be depressurized.

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: absent; interface scope requires an explicit boundary
mechanismGroups.interaction: Twelve final latches are on the CM docking ring. Electrical umbilical in LM tunnel can connect without drogue removal. CM forward pressure and thermal hatches have LM-side sockets; Tool B operates the thermal hatch socket. Three docking latches have thermal-hatch stops.

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: absent
mechanismGroups.interaction: The two stowage foldouts identify bags, containers, straps, hooks, bungees and pockets. They establish package/area placement, not a count of every zipper, latch, buckle or closure. Initial and relocated arrangements overlap.

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: absent
mechanismGroups.interaction: Stowed and deployed fabric crew-rest equipment; handbook row names hammocks but does not define attachment or deployment kinematics.

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: geometry not independently certified
mechanismGroups.interaction: Four forward handgrips and two forward-window crash bars are passive supports. No movable input should be invented for them.

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: 8 functional inputs present; exact coupled physical model not certified
mechanismGroups.interaction: Three coupled rotations and grip PTT on each right-hand controller. Longitudinal axis approximately parallel to LM X; yaw about X, pitch about Y, roll about Z. Figure 2.1-40 provides stop dimensions but no complete envelope or mounting transform.
mechanismGroups.additionalEnvelopeEvidence: controller_report Table III gives maximum external envelope, not a complete grip/base engineering drawing.
notEstablished: independent neutral cant relative to vehicle axes

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: 12 functional inputs present; exact coupled physical model not certified
mechanismGroups.interaction: One three-axis tee handle per crew station; THROTTLE/JETS selects X translation or descent throttle, retaining Y/Z translation. Friction control varies upward/downward movement force in throttle mode. Throttle response is nonlinear, with a 5-degree friction-jump interval at the breakpoint.
mechanismGroups.jetTravelCaution: Independent visual crosscheck confirms the 9.5-degree dimension spans the two bounding jet-mode travel rays, with neutral between them. It is total indicated travel, not +/-9.5 each way. Symmetric +/-4.75 endpoints are an inference and are not established here.
notEstablished: asymmetric or symmetric endpoints around jet neutral

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: not part of current 585 cockpit definitions; scope remains explicit
mechanismGroups.interaction: Stowed PLSS remote units, PLSS, OPS, helmets, purge fittings and suit hardware contain their own controls. Do not claim whole-vehicle completeness by treating them as passive bags. PLSS remote unit has fan, pump, SSC mode and volume controls plus indicators; OPS has a manual oxygen shutoff coupled to heater and a momentary heater-test switch.

mechanismGroups.inventoryStatus: portable crew-provision items absent
mechanismGroups.interaction: For LM 6 and subsequent, six 900-cc containers connect directly to PGA. Do not add the LM 5 long transfer hose and spring-loaded waste control valve to LM 7 solely because they share the preceding description and drawing.

implementationCandidates.status: PROPOSED IDs only; do not merge during live VR capture
implementationCandidates.countingCaution: Entries below are implementation functions/object states, not a newly certified physical-control denominator. Assembly proxies and multi-part mechanisms are explicitly labeled. Pose movement is an object interaction, not an extra rotary panel switch.
implementationCandidates.stateLabelsMeaning: Upper-case labels below are software state names unless sourcePlacards is explicitly true. They must not be printed as invented spacecraft placards.

cabinInputs.relationship: Deploy/unroll then engage frame snaps; release snaps before roll-up. Snap count is not sourced.
Same mechanism at overhead docking window; coordinate with COAS sightline.

Detent release required for adjustment. Source explicitly permits downward force to leave stowage; forward-area latch buttons select other positions. Do not assume one separately countable button per armrest without drawing.
LOCKED blocks rope payout, permits reeling in; do not freeze rope in both directions.

cabinInputs.range: continuous; angular end stops not sourced
cabinInputs.relationship: Clockwise raises reticle brightness. Powered by existing p8 COAS selection appropriate to mount; no numeric angle range is established.
Existing flood toggle/dimmer control emission; this mechanism changes beam aim.
Same distinction between aim and lighting power.

Distinct physical actuator from aca_cdr_ptt; route to the same crew transmission command. Held/released behavior is a functional PTT interpretation; stowage row alone supplies no stroke or contact diagram.

Press supplies water when existing ecs_des_h2o or ecs_asc_h2o feed is available (PDF446). Protective cap must be removed for use; flow is not a latching command.

scopeOrIdentityResolutionRequired.reason: Identify individual oxygen/electrical/water connector ends and retention before choosing count or IDs; ECS end remains attached in ordinary oxygen disconnect.
76 package rows do not establish every buckle, zipper or latch; no independent flight switch count can be inferred.
CM hardware accessible at LM interface; inclusion boundary and linkage data required.
Actual manual controls, not passive stowage; separate wearable/EVA inventory needed if included.
Package rows establish cameras and mounts, but not individual operation controls. Camera manuals required.

dispositionKey.mechanism: A specific movable cabin/interface mechanism is identified; see referenced mechanism group.
dispositionKey.portable: Loose article or consumable; generic pickup/stow can be modeled, but a unique flight-control input is not established.
dispositionKey.wearable: Suit/PLSS/OPS equipment with a separate wearable/EVA control scope.
dispositionKey.retention: Bag, container, strap or hose stowage; closure kinematics are not specified by this figure.
dispositionKey.passive: Fixed support or passive optical article; no movable flight input established.
dispositionKey.existing: Associated functional controls are already inventoried; this row describes the assembly or replacement article.

sourceGapLedger.established: Cylinder 92-inch diameter, 42-inch depth; stations 44 inches apart; deck approximately 36 by 55 inches. Panel angular constraints independently recorded in CONTROL-AUDIT.md.
sourceGapLedger.needed: Dimensioned station/panel drawings, not scaling the perspective stowage artwork.

sourceGapLedger.established: Every one of the 76 stowage rows has a disposition.
sourceGapLedger.needed: Assembly-level drawings for closure count, latch/zipper/buckle geometry and precise attachment locations.

sourceGapLedger.established: Stop labels, command thresholds, throttle angles and friction-force endpoints are sourced. NASA TN D-7884 supplies ACA maximum envelope and LM torque plot. Independent review reads the TTCA 9.5-degree arc as total travel, not each direction; ACA 10-degree label is soft stop, not mounting cant.
sourceGapLedger.needed: Dimensioned ACA/TTCA engineering shapes; TTCA envelope; digitized LM-specific torque/response curves; individual TTCA jet endpoints and ACA mounting transform.

sourceGapLedger.established: Portable corded/clamped lamps; overhead flood reflectors separately rotate.
sourceGapLedger.needed: Lamp/clamp dimensions and articulation limits; overhead reflector axes/ranges.

sourceGapLedger.needed: Whole mission-list reconciliation and time-dependent in-flight rearrangement if that is in simulator scope.
